exercise1.prompt: What each column is holding, and how to change it on purpose.

hiddenCases.name: text that is not a number counts as zero
an empty string counts as zero

exercise1.hint: to_numeric with errors="coerce" turns the junk into missing values, and fillna(0) then makes them zero before you sum.

questions.prompt: A column read from a CSV shows dtype object. What does that usually mean?
questions.explain: object is pandas saying "these are Python objects", which for a data file almost always means strings that have not been converted yet.

questions.prompt: What does pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce") do with "n/a"?
choices: Turns it into a missing value
questions.explain: It becomes NaN, which you then decide about -- drop it or fill it. That decision is yours rather than the parser's.

questions.prompt: Why does astype(int) fail on a column containing "n/a"?
choices: There is no integer that "n/a" means
questions.explain: astype is the strict conversion: every value has to make the trip. When some cannot, to_numeric with coerce is the tool that keeps going.
